intended_object: The element of the product module ∏ⱼ Mⱼ (a right module over ∏ⱼ Rⱼ) that is x at coordinate i and 0 elsewhere, i.e. the image of x under the canonical inclusion of the i-th factor. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: `piRight Ri Mi` is defined with `ModuleCat.of` on the plain carrier `∀ i, Mi i`, with the pointwise right action. On that carrier the body is exactly `Pi.single i x`. The only difference is that decidable equality on ι comes from `Classical.decEq ι` instead of being a hypothesis, which the docstring states. The zero on each `Mi i` is the one from its module structure, so the value is x at i and 0 elsewhere, as intended. The index type ι is arbitrary and each `Ri i` is an arbitrary ring, which is the natural generality. The definition is a thin wrapper of `Pi.single` into the library's bundled right-module product, with no unnecessary restriction and no problem in degenerate cases.
